From c7848399ec7612c2fa4dc0c2eeb9e0b89d00afef Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Florian Fainelli <f.fainelli@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Aug 2017 17:10:51 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] net: dsa: Don't dereference dst->cpu_dp->netdev

If we do not have a master network device attached dst->cpu_dp will be
NULL and accessing cpu_dp->netdev will create a trace similar to the one
below. The correct check is on dst->cpu_dp period.

Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Fixes: 6d3c8c0dd88a ("net: dsa: Remove master_netdev and use dst->cpu_dp->netdev")
Signed-off-by: Florian Fainelli <f.fainelli@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/dsa/dsa2.c b/net/dsa/dsa2.c
index c442051d5a55..20bc9c56fca0 100644
--- a/net/dsa/dsa2.c
+++ b/net/dsa/dsa2.c
@@ -577,7 +577,7 @@ static int dsa_dst_parse(struct dsa_switch_tree *dst)
 			return err;
 	}
 
-	if (!dst->cpu_dp->netdev) {
+	if (!dst->cpu_dp) {
 		pr_warn("Tree has no master device\n");
 		return -EINVAL;
 	}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/dsa/dsa2.c`**
- The condition checking for the existence of a master network device was modified. 
- The original line `if (!dst->cpu_dp->netdev)` was changed to `if (!dst->cpu_dp)`. 
- This change prevents dereferencing `dst->cpu_dp` when it is `NULL`, which avoids potential kernel NULL pointer dereference errors.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug reported by Dan Carpenter, which indicated that dereferencing `dst->cpu_dp` when it is `NULL` leads to a kernel panic. 
- The change is a direct fix to the issue introduced by a previous commit (identified by the hash `6d3c8c0dd88a`), which incorrectly assumed that `dst->cpu_dp` would always be valid. 
- By checking `dst->cpu_dp` directly instead of its `netdev` member, the patch ensures that the code safely handles cases where no master network device is attached, thus improving the stability of the DSA (Distributed Switch Architecture) implementation.
